key_insight: The paper introduces a stabilized augmented mixed finite element formulation for the nonlinear Biot poroelasticity problem, coupling stress, displacement, pressure, and rotation with a fixed-point treatment of nonlinear permeability.
engineering_relevance: It provides a mathematically well-posed and error-controlled framework for simulating coupled flow-deformation processes in porous media, which is important for geomechanics, subsurface engineering, and poromechanical design.
method: Augment the mixed Biot equations with suitable stabilization terms to ensure well-posedness.
Use a fixed-point strategy to handle the nonlinear permeability and prove existence/uniqueness.
Develop a finite element discretization with discrete solvability, a priori error estimates, and residual-based a posteriori estimators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis plus two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments to assess performance, including reliability and efficiency of the residual estimator.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully chosen stabilization parameters and fixed-point convergence, so practical implementation may be sensitive to parameter selection and nonlinear solve robustness.
paper_title: An augmented mixed finite element method for the Biot problem with nonlinear permeability
